# Orbital Strike does nothing

## Problem statement

The **Orbital Strike** power-up is functionally wired but reads to the player as
doing nothing: it produces **no sound at all** and reuses the generic Smart Bomb
AOE ring instead of an orbital bolt, so nothing about it says "an orbital strike
just happened". Worse, in the two most common situations the bolt is **silently
consumed with zero feedback** — no VFX, no SFX, no damage.

## Users

As a **player**, I want picking up an Orbital Strike to produce an unmistakable
event — a bolt falling from the sky onto the target with its own sound — so that
I can tell the power-up is working, and so that the permanent (hold-full) reward
is worth the choice.

As a **player**, I do not want a pickup wasted silently when it is collected
while no enemy is alive; I want the strike to land on the next target (or be
clearly signalled as unused).

## Existing state (repo research)

The power-up is **not** dead code — the damage path exists and is tested. What is
missing is the *feedback layer* plus two silent-failure paths.

1. **State + decision (working).** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` sets
   `_strikePulsePending = true` for a field pickup and `_strikePermanent = true`
   + a pulse timer for a hold-full reward (`src/powerups/effects.ts:644`).
   `EffectsRegistry.updateStrike(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1241`) returns
   `true` exactly once for a queued pickup and then once per
   `strikeInterval()` (`max(10, 30 − 2×level)` s) for the permanent reward.
2. **Shared detection (working).** `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike`
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1655`) is called from `_tickPlayer`
   (`:878`) and forwards to the `onOrbitalStrike(damage)` hook, so the game and
   every gym run one implementation.
3. **Application (working, but visually generic).**
   `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:642`) picks the
   live enemy nearest the ship, then spawns
   `spawnNovaRing(..., ORBITAL_STRIKE_RADIUS = 40, ORBITAL_STRIKE_COLOR = 0x9ffcff)`
   plus `spawnBulletImpact(...)` and applies `damageEnemyViaAoe(target, damage)`.
   That is **the same nova-ring helper and colour family as the Smart Bomb
   pulse** (`onSmartBombPulse`, `CombatScene.ts:673`) — there is no descending
   bolt, no target marker, no telegraph, no screen flash/shake. The ring lasts
   `NOVA_RING_DURATION = 0.5` s (`src/vfx/aoeEffect.ts:25`), so it is easy to miss
   entirely during play.
4. **No SFX exists.** `src/audio/effects.ts` exports **no** orbital-strike cue
   and `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (66 cues) has **no** strike entry. The
   `onOrbitalStrike` body makes no `play*` call. The unrelated Missile-Command
   **hazard** entity (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) borrows
   `playScoutAdvanceCue` (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md:94`), which is
   why the hazard is audible and the power-up is silent.
5. **Silent-waste path A — no target.** `onOrbitalStrike` returns early when no
   live enemy is found (`CombatScene.ts:646`), but `updateStrike` has **already**
   cleared `_strikePulsePending`. A pickup collected between waves is therefore
   consumed with literally no effect: "it does nothing at all".
6. **Silent-waste path B — no player.** `_updateOrbitalStrike` does not guard on
   a live player; `onOrbitalStrike` does. Same silent consumption.
7. **Weak readout.** The HUD shows a `strike` row **only** while the strike is
   permanent (`src/ui/HUD.ts:523`) and never shows the time to the next bolt, so
   even an armed permanent strike looks inert.
8. **Damage is often invisible.** `strikeDamage()` is `1` hit at level 1
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:979`), so a bolt on a multi-HP enemy removes
   one pip and on a 1-HP grunt is indistinguishable from an ordinary bullet kill.

## Desired change

Give Orbital Strike a distinct, legible identity and remove the silent failures:

- A **descending orbital bolt** (beam/column from off-screen top down to the
  target) ending in a bright impact flash — its own VFX module, not the Smart
  Bomb ring.
- A **new dedicated SFX cue** (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV), played at the
  bolt's impact.
- **No silent consumption**: a queued bolt with no live target (or no live
  player) is **retained** and fired on the first valid frame rather than being
  discarded.
- The HUD `strike` row shows the countdown to the next bolt for a permanent
  strike.

> Scope confirmed by the producer (2026-10-28): this work item covers the
> **power-up** only; the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` hazard is out of scope
> except for non-regression (AC7).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct visual identity.** A strike (field pickup or permanent pulse)
   renders a descending bolt from the top of the play area onto the target plus
   an impact flash, through a new VFX module in `src/vfx/`, and the visual is
   demonstrably distinct from the Smart Bomb pulse (different shape/composition,
   not just a recoloured `spawnNovaRing`), asserted by unit tests on the module.
2. **Dedicated audio cue.** A new `playOrbitalStrikeSound` cue exists in
   `src/audio/effects.ts`, backed by a **new** ToneForge recipe
   (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV built via `scripts/build-audio.sh`),
   registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, and played by the shared strike
   path; `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` and `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`
   stay green.
3. **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live
   player) is present is **not** lost: the queued bolt is **retained** and lands
   on the first frame with a valid target. A regression test drives a pickup with
   no live enemy and asserts the bolt subsequently lands on the next live enemy.
   At most one bolt is retained (a permanent strike simply resumes its interval)
   so a long enemy-free gap cannot bank a volley.
4. **Damage path unchanged.** The bolt still applies `strikeDamage()` hits to the
   nearest live enemy through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, and still depletes enemy force
   fields through the shared `takeDamage()` seam —
   `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` stay green.
5. **Gym↔game parity.** The VFX/SFX and the no-silent-waste behaviour live once
   in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and are consumed by `PlayScene` and
   every gym; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body
   guard) and a gym parity test in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`
   stay green, and the strike is observable in the gym.
6. **HUD countdown.** A permanent strike's HUD row shows a live countdown
   (`next in Ns`) to the next bolt, asserted by a HUD test.
7. **Hazard reviewed, not regressed.** The unrelated Missile-Command
   `orbital-strike` hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) is confirmed
   unaffected by this change; its suite (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` §"Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike")
   stays green.
8. **Testing/validation.** Every acceptance criterion above is covered by an
   automated test that fails before the change and passes after it.
9. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — including code comments, the GDD §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section
   (following the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" precedent, which documents
   the aura and cue beside the mechanics), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
   for the new cue, and any relevant README or wiki entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory.** No divergent copy: shared behaviour in
  `src/scenes/core/` (and shared dispatchers), consumed by `PlayScene` and every
  gym scene. Any intentional divergence must be recorded in this work item and in
  a code comment.
- **Audio goes through the cue pipeline.** A cue may not be synthesised ad hoc:
  it needs a `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` entry plus a recipe under
  `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, and (for `baked` delivery) a rebuilt WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`. The contract suite asserts every `play*` export is
  manifested.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- Cosmetic/feel work only — do **not** re-tune strike damage, interval or drop
  weight as part of this change unless a tuning defect is found (record it as
  linked follow-up work instead).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onOrbitalStrike`: replace the generic
  `spawnNovaRing` composition with the new bolt VFX and the new cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateOrbitalStrike`: retain/requeue a
  bolt when no target or no player is available (the no-silent-waste seam).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `updateStrike`: expose a requeue/retain path so a
  decided bolt is not lost.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts` — **New.** Descending bolt + impact-flash VFX,
  registered like `src/vfx/thornsAbsorb.ts` / `aoeEffect.ts`.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.test.ts` — **New.** VFX composition/distinctness tests.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **New** `playOrbitalStrikeSound` wrapper.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `audio/toneforge/recipes/` — **New** cue
  entry (`aihell-orbital-strike`) and recipe.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — document the new cue row.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `next in Ns` countdown on the permanent `strike` row (AC6).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section: strike
  visibility + cue paragraph.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — gym parity + observability test.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (now confirmed):** "Orbital Strike" in the report means the
  **power-up** (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.strike`, display name exactly "Orbital
  Strike"), not the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` **hazard**. Confirmed by the
  producer (Q1 → (a)); the hazard is out of scope except for non-regression
  (AC7). Rationale: the hazard already has a telegraph, a falling shell, a
  detonation burst and a borrowed cue, whereas the power-up has no cue at all.
- **Risk — new audio asset cost.** A new dedicated recipe plus a WAV rebuild is
  required (Q2 → new strike SFX). This is the largest single risk: the ToneForge
  recipe must be authored, baked and manifested, and the baked asset must survive
  the audio balance guard. Budgeted as its own WBS item.
- **Risk — VFX legibility vs. visual noise.** A full-height bolt on every pulse
  may fight other screen effects; cap its draw to the target column and keep the
  duration short, and validate in `GymPowerUpsCombat` with a live player.
- **Risk — retarget semantics.** Retaining a queued bolt could stack up several
  bolts during a long enemy-free gap. AC3 caps the retained queue at one bolt (a
  permanent strike simply resumes its interval) so the behaviour stays
  predictable and testable.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Levelling, drop-weight and interval tuning, a strike
  "charging" telegraph, and multi-target strikes are all tempting; they are
  **out of scope** and should be captured as linked follow-up work items rather
  than absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** the "[no] VFX" complaint refers to the *generic, unnoticeable*
  ring rather than a rendering defect — no rendering bug was found in research.

## Related work

- **Some power-ups appear to do nothing (AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z)** — wired this
  power-up's gameplay consumers (commit `154b7adb`); AC5 covered damage only, not
  VFX/SFX.
- **Orbital Strike substrate (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue, level curves,
  effects-registry accessors and HUD readouts for the net-new power-ups.
- **Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1)** — the
  unrelated enemy hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`); reviewed for
  non-regression only.
- **Orbital-Strike falling shell projectile identity (AH-0MV822GIO005B685)** —
  the hazard projectile's visual identity; a useful precedent for giving the
  power-up its own identity.
- **Create E4 Phaser gym scene (AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13)** / Phaser orbital work —
  unrelated (`orbital` formation kind, not this power-up).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 (power-up levels, Orbital Strike row) and
  the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" paragraph in the same section — the
  documentation precedent for describing a power-up's VFX/SFX.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — the cue catalogue the new sound must
  join.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which "Orbital Strike" does this report mean: the power-up or the
  campaign hazard?**
  Options: (a) the **power-up** (`strike`, "Orbital Strike" pickup/choice
  reward); (b) the Missile-Command **hazard** (`orbital-strike` enemy entity);
  (c) both.
  **Recommended:** (a) the power-up — it has literally no SFX and only a
  borrowed generic AOE ring, which matches "no VFX or SFX".
  — **Answer (producer): (a) the power-up** — the `strike` power-up
  ("Orbital Strike"). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. The Missile-Command
  `orbital-strike` **hazard** is therefore **out of scope**, reviewed for
  non-regression only (AC7). Research evidence supporting the answer: the
  power-up has zero audio cues and a generic 0.5 s ring; the hazard has a
  telegraph, a falling shell, a detonation burst and the borrowed
  `playScoutAdvanceCue`.

- **Q2 — May we add a new baked SFX cue, or must we reuse an existing one?**
  Options: (a) **new dedicated recipe** (`aihell-orbital-strike`) + baked WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; (b) **reuse an existing electric recipe** (e.g.
  `aihell-arc-fire`) with no new asset; (c) no new audio, make the visual carry
  the identity.
  **Recommended:** (a) a new dedicated recipe — an orbital strike is a signature
  event and should not share a cue with the arc weapon.
  — **Answer (producer): a new dedicated strike SFX cue** — option (a). Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-10-28. Binding constraint: the cue needs a new ToneForge
  recipe (proposed slug `aihell-orbital-strike`) plus a baked WAV built via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`,
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and the audio contract tests
  (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`) must be
  updated in the same change.

- **Q3 — Should the permanent strike's HUD row show a countdown to the next
  bolt?**
  Options: (a) yes, add `next in Ns`; (b) no, keep the row as-is.
  **Recommended:** (a) yes — a 10–30 s interval is otherwise invisible, and the
  HUD already renders countdowns for other timed effects.
  — **Answer (producer): (a) yes** — add a `next in Ns` countdown to the
  permanent strike's HUD row. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. AC6 is now a
  required criterion rather than an optional one.

- **Q4 — Is it acceptable that the strike retains a queued bolt when no enemy is
  alive (rather than being wasted)?**
  **Recommended:** yes — silently losing a rare pickup is the reported bug.
  — **Answer (producer): yes, retain the bolt** — a queued bolt is retained and
  lands on the first frame with a valid target. Source: interactive reply,

  "signal as unused" path.

# Test: setup field contracts and arc table (test-first)

Test-first verification slice for the scripted-video arc (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB; covers parent AC5 and the determinism half of AC4). This item writes the failing tests that specify the new scene-`setup` fields and the seven-beat example table **before** any implementation lands, so the behaviour is pinned by tests rather than by prose.

**Test-first rule:** every test in this item must be written and observed failing (for the right reason: unknown setup field / missing behaviour) before F2, F3 and F4 turn them green. Do not weaken an assertion to make it pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — New setup fields are parsed and validated.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` covers `setup.player.weaponLevels`, `setup.bossHitsRemaining` and `setup.mineralReward`: accepted shapes parse; wrong shapes raise the documented error codes; normalisation yields documented defaults; re-normalising a normalised setup is idempotent (deep-equal).
- **AC2 — Validation is target-aware.** A field is rejected on a target that cannot consume it (`unknown-setup-field` for an unknown name, `setup-not-supported`/`unsupported-setup-field`-style code for a known-but-unsupported field on that target), and `bossHitsRemaining` is accepted only on the boss-capable targets (`GymBoss`, `GymMiniBoss`). Out-of-range values (e.g. `0`, negative, non-integer, above the entity's total HP) are rejected with a documented code.
- **AC3 — Applier behaviour is specified.** `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` asserts with a fake player that `player.weaponLevels: { rapid: 3 }` produces three permanent `equipWeapon('rapid', true)` calls (level N == N permanent grants), that `player.weapons` still grants level 1, and that a forced `mineralReward` selects the named reward instead of a random one.
- **AC4 — Boss hit preview is specified.** A test asserts that `bossHitsRemaining` reaches the spawned boss/mini-boss as `initialHp` (spawn-path unit test against `GymBoss`/`GymMiniBoss` seams), and that an absent field leaves today's full-HP spawn unchanged.
- **AC5 — The seven-beat arc table is pinned.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (or a dedicated `examples/scenes.json` table test) asserts the exact seven entries: beat order, `target`, `playMs`/`captureMs` window presence, `label`, per-scene seed, `player.weaponLevels`/`player.weapons` and slot counts, `bossHitsRemaining` on the mini-boss and boss beats, and `mineralReward` on the humble-origins beat. Scene 6 (reprise) is asserted to differ from scene 4 in both enemy mix and player weapons, so a copy-paste edit cannot collapse the two beats.
- **AC6 — Doc parity is specified.** `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` asserts `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents each new setup field (two-way parity with the parser's field list) and each new error code, and that the shipped example parses. (The doc additions themselves land in F5.)
- **AC7 — No test is vacuous.** Every new test asserts observable behaviour (returned value, thrown code, or call list); no test merely asserts a constant equals itself.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` — parser/validator/normaliser/idempotence/error-code tests and the arc table assertions.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — applier tests for weapon levels and forced reward.
- `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` — doc↔schema two-way parity assertions.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — read-only reference for the existing field list and error codes.

## Dependencies

# Test: cross-scene spawn/fire/march parity for the level-launch path (red-before)

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC1, AC2, AC3). **Test-first item — create and land the failing tests before any production change.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want a cross-scene equivalence test that boots `PlayScene` and the
level-launch gym (`GymLevel`, and `GymBotTuning` through inheritance) with the *same* seeded wave
and asserts identical spawn transit, identical fire cadence and identical march motion, so a
future divergence in the spawn seam cannot land without the suite failing.

## Problem

Parity coverage today exists for `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and
`GymFodderEnemies` (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for the
level-launch path. `GymLevel.test.ts` even works around the missing `shootEnabled` hand-off by
setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand, which is itself part of the defect.

## Required behaviour (the assertions that must exist)

1. **Orbital transit destination (AC1).** For an orbital wave (the Phaser), every frame of the
   wormhole spawn window in `GymLevel` must resolve a destination equal to the entity's live
   `formationSlot()` — asserted frame by frame against the same wave driven through `PlayScene`.
   No frame may place the Phaser on the straight grid line `startX + driftX + col*spacingX`, and
   the landing position at the end of the window must equal the orbital slot (no snap).
2. **Fire cadence (AC2).** A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` must produce the same number
   of bullets, at the same `scene.time.now` ticks, with the same bullet speed, in `GymLevel` /
   `GymBotTuning` as in `PlayScene`. The test must **not** set `shootEnabled` by hand — it must
   flow from the wave definition (`src/waves/Formations.ts`, campaign levels 4+).
3. **March block (AC3).** For a `march` wave, stepping through an identical `dt` sequence must
   produce the same base position (x, y, direction) and the same per-member offsets in `GymLevel`
   as `PlayScene`'s `marchState` block, including at least one edge reversal and one drop.

## Implementation guidance

- Put the new coverage in `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` (already the level-gym parity home,
  AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) unless the file becomes unwieldy, in which case add
  `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` and keep the level-parity file for scaling/cadence.
- Reuse the existing `bootScene` harness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) and the existing cross-scene
  equivalence patterns in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — do not invent a second harness.
- Express the wave with a fixed seed so both scenes see identical content (the `sceneSetup` seed
  seam, `resolveSetupSeed`). No `Math.random`.
- Mark the new assertions with Vitest `it.fails(...)` (the repo's red-before/green-after
  convention, cf. `levelParity.test.ts` header) **or** `it(...)` with an explicit
  `// red-before: fails until AH-<child-of-this-item> lands` note, and flip them to `it` in the
  fix item. Whichever convention the surrounding file already uses must be followed.
- The flip-to-green work belongs to the implementation children (shared seam
  AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN, then the `GymLevel` parity fix AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B). This item is complete
  as soon as the tests exist and demonstrably fail on the pre-fix HEAD; the red-before markers are
  flipped by AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B.

## Red-before evidence

Record in a comment: the exact failing assertion output on pre-fix HEAD (all three assertions),
plus the commit hash of the test-only commit. This is the reproducibility proof the parent ACs
require.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A cross-scene test asserts, frame by frame, that `GymLevel`'s orbital spawn
  destination equals the live `formationSlot()` for every frame of the spawn window, and that the
  end-of-window position equals the orbital slot; it fails on pre-fix HEAD and the failure output
  is recorded on this item.
- [ ] AC2 — A cross-scene test asserts identical post-spawn fire cadence, bullet count and bullet
  speed for a wave with `shootEnabled: true` in `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` vs `PlayScene`, without
  any hand-set `shootEnabled`; it fails on pre-fix HEAD (zero bullets in the gym) and the output is
  recorded.
- [ ] AC3 — A cross-scene test drives an identical `dt` sequence through a `march` wave and
  asserts identical base position, direction and member offsets in the gym vs `PlayScene`,
  including one edge reversal and one drop; it fails on pre-fix HEAD and the output is recorded.
- [ ] AC4 — `GymBotTuning` is covered by inheritance or an explicit assertion (the reported
  symptom was observed in `GymBotTuning`, which extends `GymLevel`).
- [ ] AC5 — No production file is modified by this item (tests and test helpers only), and the
  pre-existing suite stays green apart from the new red-before assertions.

- AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after). — **contribution:** this item delivers the red-before cross-scene test half (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the red-before cadence test half (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the red-before march test half (see Parent AC coverage below).

# Gym↔game parity sweep of all 14 gym scenes and published parity matrix

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC5, first half).

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want a single published matrix that records, for every gym scene, which
shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and
where it diverges and why — so the parity claim is auditable instead of assumed.

## Scope — every gym must appear

All scenes under `src/scenes/gym/` (14, including the generic base and the level/bot-tuning path):

`GymBoss`, `GymBotTuning`, `GymCentipede`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`,
`GymMinerals`, `GymMiniBoss`, `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`,
`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymWeapons`
— plus the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` as its own row.

## What the sweep must check, per gym

1. **Enabled gameplay objects** — which entities, weapons, power-ups, drops, minerals and hazards
   are live, and whether each runs the shipped code (shared core / shared helper / shared entity)
   or a gym-local implementation.
2. **Start-of-wave / spawn path** — which spawn seam the gym uses (shared core template, shared
   `spawnTransit` seam, `GymLevel.spawnWave`, in-place), whether wormhole presentation is the
   shared one, and whether transit destination/`shootEnabled`/march are honoured.
3. **Combat inheritance** — whether the gym derives from `CombatScene` / `CombatCoreScene` /
   `GymFormationScene` (and therefore inherits the shipped update/collision/fire/drop loops) or
   runs its own loop.
4. **Divergences** — every intentional divergence with its documented reason and the file/section
   that records it. Expected intentional divergences to re-justify (do not "fix" them):
   `GymPlayer`'s obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE `TrainingTarget`s, the flat supply cadence in
   `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels, and the absence of run telemetry.
5. **Classification** — each row gets a verdict: `parity`, `intentional divergence (reason)`, or
   `divergence to fix`. Anything marked `divergence to fix` is handed to the sibling fix item; every
   row must end up `parity` or `intentional divergence`.

## Deliverable

A new `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` containing:

- A table with one row per gym scene: scene | derives from | enabled shipped objects | spawn seam |
  combat loop inherited | verdict | reason / evidence (file:line).
- A short "how to re-audit" section saying which seams are guarded automatically
  (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` / `EPIC_SHARED_METHODS`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`) and which are
  human-reviewed, so the next sweep is cheap.
- An explicit statement that `PlayScene` is the reference and that the game must never be changed to
  match a gym.

Add a docs guard (extend `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` or a sibling test) that fails if a
gym scene exists under `src/scenes/gym/` without a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, so the matrix cannot
rot as gyms are added.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records every gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (14 scenes plus the
  generic `GymFormationScene` row), with enabled shipped objects, spawn seam, combat-loop
  inheritance and verdict per row.
- [ ] AC2 — Every divergence is classified `intentional divergence (<reason + evidence>)` or
  `divergence to fix`; all five known intentional divergences are re-justified with a file/section
  reference and no intentional divergence is "fixed" by this item.
- [ ] AC3 — An automated guard fails if a `Gym*.ts` production scene under `src/scenes/gym/` has no
  row in the matrix (red-before demonstrated by adding a temporary scene or by asserting against a
  fixture, then green).
- [ ] AC4 — Every `divergence to fix` row is recorded with enough evidence (file:line, observed vs
  expected, reproduction steps) for the sibling fix item to act on without re-auditing.
- [ ] AC5 — The audit itself introduces no behaviour change: production code is untouched apart from
  the docs guard test; the suite stays green.
- [ ] AC6 — The sweep explicitly reports on the three known spawn divergences (orbital transit,
  `shootEnabled`, march) as fixed-by-sibling or still-open, so the matrix agrees with the fix item.

- AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC6, second half — configuration/automation contract). **Blocked by
the setup-adoption item AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8** so the fields it declares actually exist in the
scenes.

## Goal / user story

As a producer, I want to write a gym scenario in `examples/scenes.json` (gym key + setup + scenario
parameters) and have the capture CLI accept it, validate it clearly, launch it and record it — and
get a clear, actionable error when I ask for something the scene cannot do.

## Current state

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` owns config parsing/validation, `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (12 gyms),
  `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`), `SCENE_SETUP_INCAPABLE_TARGETS`,
  `SCENE_SETUP_TARGET_EXTRA_FIELDS`, `SCENE_SETUP_COMMON_FIELDS` and
  `sceneSetupFieldsFor` / `requiredSceneSetupFieldsFor` / `isKnownSceneKey`.
- `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` deliberately excludes `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel` (they need a
  launch parameter), and the registry is pinned by `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` plus a docs
  assertion in `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts`.
- `examples/scenes.json` demonstrates scripted scenes but no gym scenario with per-gym parameters.

## Desired change

1. **Schema.** Extend the scene config so a gym entry can carry its scenario parameters (enemy
   roster, formation, launched level, toggles) alongside the existing common setup fields
   (`seed`, `player`, `powerUps`). Keep the common fields common; declare per-gym extras in
   `SCENE_SETUP_TARGET_EXTRA_FIELDS`.
2. **Validation.** `sceneSetupFieldsFor` / the validator must:
   - accept a setup for **every** gym (no remaining `SCENE_SETUP_INCAPABLE_TARGETS` gym, unless a
     documented reason exists — re-justify each removal or retention in the matrix and capture docs);
   - reject an unsupported field on a gym with a clear, actionable error carrying a stable
     `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES` code (name the offending field and list the fields the target
     accepts);
   - require the launch parameter for parameterised targets and reject one supplied to a
     non-parameterised target.
3. **Registry contract.** Update `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` and
   their pinning test so the registry matches reality: every gym is either watchable directly or
   watchable-with-required-parameter, and the pinning test asserts the exhaustive partition (no gym
   missing, none in both, none unknown).
4. **Examples.** Add at least one scripted gym scenario per gym family to `examples/scenes.json`
   (formation family, level/bot-tuning, player, weapons, power-ups, leveling, minerals, centipede,
   mini-boss, boss, curve sequencer) with the parameters they now accept, and a documented
   copy-paste snippet in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
5. **Docs.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` gains a section on gym scenarios: the accepted fields per
   gym, the required launch parameter, and one working example.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` validates gym scenario parameters for every gym, with
  per-gym extra fields declared in `SCENE_SETUP_TARGET_EXTRA_FIELDS` and no gym silently dropping a
  supplied field.
- [ ] AC2 — The validator rejects an unsupported field, a missing required launch parameter, and a
  launch parameter on a non-parameterised target, each with a stable error code, an actionable
  message and a test.
- [ ] AC3 — `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` exhaustively partition the
  gyms; the pinning test (`scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`) and the docs assertion
  (`src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts`) are updated and pass.
- [ ] AC4 — `examples/scenes.json` contains a working scripted entry for each gym family (≥ 8
  entries covering all 14 scenes, parameterised ones included) and the config validates in CI.
- [ ] AC5 — A dry-run/validation test proves each `examples/scenes.json` gym entry resolves to a

  - a **descending bolt** — a tapered, glowing column that tweens from above the top of the play area down to the target, drawn **only** in the target's column (no full-screen wash);

**As a designer**, I want the campaign-wide variety rules expressed as one shared, pure analysis module with automated tests, so future wave edits cannot silently reintroduce sequential repetition (parent AC1–AC3).

This feature delivers the *measurement* first: the shared audit module and the failing invariant tests that define "more variation" precisely, before any wave data or generator changes land. Everything else in the epic reuses this module rather than reimplementing composition logic.

## What to build

1. A new pure module `src/waves/campaignVariety.ts` (no Phaser/runtime import) exporting:
   - `waveComposition(wave)` — sorted, de-duplicated archetype-key signature of a wave, counting **wave groups and spawner opt-in flags** (`ghosts` → `GHOST_ENEMY_KEYS`, `centipede` → `CENTIPEDE_ENEMY_KEY`, `horde` → `GRUNT_ENEMY_KEY`, `laneTraffic` → `LANE_TRAFFIC_ENEMY_KEY`), mirroring the existing `keysInWave` helper in `campaignInvariants.test.ts`.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
**test-first (red) item** for the wheel overlay scene; the paired
implementation item is "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene".

## Summary

Author scene tests for the wheel overlay **before** the scene exists, pinning
the launcher-agnostic contract, the spin animation contract and the
"applied exactly once" invariant, so the implementation is driven by tests.

## What the tests must pin

- **Wedges** — one wedge per owned permanent kind across the shared six-slot
  pool (power-up kinds **and** weapon drops) plus a single **bonus** wedge;
  icons come from the existing code-drawn `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon`
  (no external art assets).
- **Launch contract** — the scene is launched with `wedges` (the resolved
  wedge list derived by the launcher from the owned-kind snapshot), a resolved
  `outcome` (which wedge to land on + any extra gains) and a **single
  optional** result callback mirroring `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`; the scene
  never reaches back into any launcher by key and never computes probabilities.
- **Spin is player-initiated** — pointer click and any keyboard key start the
  spin; nothing applies an outcome before a spin (except the demo auto-spin).
- **Animation** — the spin starts fast and eases out (≈2.2 s total, at most one
  overshoot revolution, the duration exported as a constant so a test can pin
  it); the pointer stops on the wedge supplied by the outcome; the landed wedge
  is highlighted.
- **Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer, 2026-10-28)** — the landing wedge of
  a multi-upgrade outcome renders **all** the gained kinds' icons inside that
  one wedge ("all icons present"); extra gained kinds are **not** lit up on
  separate wedges; the whole outcome still applies exactly once.
- **Exactly once** — the result callback fires exactly once per spin; a second
  click/key press or a repeated spin after resolution is a no-op.
- **Demo auto-spin** — with `autoSpinMs` set (> 0) the scene spins after that
  delay; unset → it waits indefinitely for input.

## Landing (test-first pair)

Same branch as its paired implementation item: tests committed first (red for
the right reason, recorded) and the pair closed together once green. Red tests
